332407.title: Conjectured decomposition of level-$k$ Dyck vectors
332407.literal_statement:
Fix an integer $k
geq 0$. For each $n
geq 0$ and each $\mu
iu
a\text{Par}(k)$, let $\mathcal{DV}_{n,k}$ denote the set of level-$k$ Dyck vectors of length $n$. For a partition $\lambda$, $\textsc{dyck}(\lambda)$ is the associated Dyck vector, and $\lambda'$ is its conjugate partition. Two subsets are **opposite** when corresponding objects have their area and dinv interchanged. The map $\iota_n$ is the injection from the stated inclusion of Dyck-vector sets.

**Conjectured decomposition.** There exist possibly identical subsets $\mathcal{DV}_{n,\mu}$ and $\overline{\mathcal{DV}}_{n,\mu}$ of $\mathcal{DV}_{n,k}$ such that: (a) each of the two families, indexed by $\mu
iu
\operatorname{Par}(k)$, is a disjoint partition of $\mathcal{DV}_{n,k}$; (b) $\mathcal{DV}_{n,\mu}$ and $\overline{\mathcal{DV}}_{n,\mu}$ are opposite; (c) membership of $\textsc{dyck}(\lambda)$ in the first implies membership of $\textsc{dyck}(\lambda')$ in the second; (d) the injection $\iota_n$ maps each family into its corresponding family at level $n+1$; and (e) both family sizes tend to infinity as $n$ tends to infinity.

332420.title: Characterization of fixed ordering configurations by formal expansion fixedness
332420.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a set of point labels and $\mathcal{B}$ a set of coordinate indices. A linear ordering configuration $\mathcal{C}$ on $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B})$ is **fixed** when the sign or non-nullity of $det(M_{\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B}})$ is determined by the prescribed coordinate orderings. It is **formally fixed by expansion** when some cofactor expansion of $det(M_{\mathcal{E},\mathcal{B}})$ with respect to a pair $(e_i,e_j)$ has formal sign $\fbox{+}$ or $\fbox{-}$, using the signs of the induced lower-dimensional determinants. **Expansion characterization conjecture.** The configuration $\mathcal{C}$ is fixed if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ is formally fixed by expansion. The implication from formal expansion fixedness to fixedness is established, but the converse is presented as a conjecture in the supplied text.

332887.title: Holographic renormalization conjecture for bulk Laplacian eigenvalue variation
332887.literal_statement:
Let $(X,G)$ be the bulk with boundary $M$, and let $\tilde{D}=-\Delta_G$ and $D=-\Delta_g$ be the bulk and boundary Laplace--Beltrami operators, respectively. Here $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $\tilde{D}$, $\rho$ is the holographic renormalization parameter, and $\zeta(s,D)$ is the spectral zeta function of $D$. **Holographic eigenvalue-variation conjecture.** In the geometric setup of the AdS/CFT correspondence, holographic renormalization gives

$$
\frac{\partial \lambda}{\partial \rho}=-\frac{1}{2}\zeta'(0,D)+\rho\zeta(0,D).
$$

In the first-term approximation, this becomes

$$
\frac{\partial \lambda}{\partial \rho}=-\frac{1}{2}\zeta'(0,D).
$$

The claim connects spectral data of the boundary Laplacian with the variation of bulk eigenvalues and is motivated by the relation between thermal entropy, free energy, and holographic renormalization in odd-dimensional bulk geometry. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

332892.title: The Cauchy-Davenport constant inequality for cancellative semigroups
332892.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb A$ be a cancellative semigroup with underlying set $A$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n\subseteq A$. For each tuple, let $\gamma(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ denote its Cauchy-Davenport constant, defined by $\gamma(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=0$ if some $X_i$ is empty and otherwise $\gamma(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\gamma(X_i)$, where $\gamma(X)=|X|$ for $|X|\leq 1$ and, otherwise, $\gamma(X)=\sup_{x_0\in X^\times}\inf_{x_0\neq x\in X}\operatorname{ord}(x-x_0)$. **The Cauchy-Davenport constant inequality.** One should have

$$
|X_1+\cdots+X_n|\geq\min\bigl(\gamma(X_1,\ldots,X_n),|X_1|+\cdots+|X_n|+1-n\bigr).
$$

This is a proposed extension of Cauchy-Davenport type lower bounds from groups to cancellative semigroups; the source attributes the proposal to earlier work and asks whether it can be proved or disproved. Its resolution is not established in the supplied material.

333265.title: Completeness conjecture for Legendrian graph stabilizations and vertex twists
333265.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $g:G\rightarrow S^3$ be a smooth embedding. A **Legendrian realization** of $g$ is a Legendrian embedding of $G$ in $(S^3,\xi_{std})$ representing the smooth embedding $g$. **Legendrian graph equivalence conjecture.** Any two Legendrian realizations $g_1$ and $g_2$ of $g$ are related, up to Legendrian isotopy, by a sequence of edge stabilizations, vertex stabilizations, and vertex twists.

Edge stabilization, vertex stabilization, and vertex twist are local operations on Legendrian graphs that preserve their smooth isotopy class. The conjecture proposes that these operations completely classify Legendrian realizations within a fixed smooth isotopy class; the preceding discussion explains that edge stabilizations alone are insufficient, while no resolution is given here.

333319.title: The hypercellular complex characterization conjecture
333319.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **hyperprism complex** is a polyhedral cell complex whose cells are Cartesian products of segments and regular polygons with an even number of sides, glued so that the intersection of any two cells is a cell; its 1-skeleton is the graph formed by its 0-cells and 1-cells. A **hypercellular complex** is a cell complex of a hypercellular graph. A polygonal complex is a complex whose 2-cells are regular polygons with an even number of sides. The 3C-condition and 3CC-condition are the corresponding conditions described in the paper.

**The hypercellular complex characterization conjecture.** For a graph $G$, the following conditions are equivalent:

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(i)} & G \text{ is hypercellular};\\
\text{(ii)} & G \text{ is the 1-skeleton of a simply connected hyperprism complex }{\bf X}\text{ satisfying the 3C-condition};\\
\text{(iii)} & G \text{ is the 1-skeleton of a simply connected polygonal complex }{\bf X}\text{ whose 2-cells are regular polygons with an even number of sides and which satisfies the 3CC-condition}.
\end{array}
$$

Moreover, all hypercellular cell complexes are CAT(0) spaces. This would provide a geometric characterization extending the analogous characterization of median graphs by simply connected cube complexes satisfying the cube condition. It would also imply the fixed point property used earlier in the paper, but the conjecture is not resolved in the supplied text.

333754.title: Bilinear relation for generic q-deformed conformal blocks
333754.literal_statement:
Let $q_1,q_2,u,Z$ satisfy $|q_2|<1<|q_1|$. Define

$$
\widehat{\mathcal{F}}_d(u,q_1,q_2|Z)=\sum_{2n\in\mathbb{Z}}\frac{u^{2dn}(q_1q_2)^{4dn^2}Z^{2n^2}}{(uq_1^{4n-2},u^{-1}q_1^{-4n-2})^{(1)}_\infty(uq_1^{-1}q_2^{4n+1},u^{-1}q_1^{-1}q_2^{-4n+1})^{(2)}_\infty}\mathcal{F}^{(1)}_n(q_1^{2d}Z)\mathcal{F}^{(2)}_n(q_2^{2d}Z),
$$

where

$$
\mathcal{F}^{(1)}_n(z)=\mathcal{F}(uq_1^{4n},q_1^2,q_1^{-1}q_2|z),\qquad \mathcal{F}^{(2)}_n(z)=\mathcal{F}(uq_2^{4n},q_1q_2^{-1},q_2^2|z).
$$

Also define

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\lozenge}(u,q_1,q_2|Z)=\sum_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}Z^{\frac{|\lambda_1|+|\lambda_2|}{2}}\frac{1}{\prod_{i,j=1}^2N^{\mathrm{NS}}_{\lambda_i,\lambda_j}(q_1,q_2,u_i/u_j)}.
$$

The source defines the factors $N^{\lozenge}_{\lambda,\mu}$ using the subsets of boxes selected by the stated parity condition.

**Generic bilinear relation.**

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\lozenge}(u,q_1,q_2|Z)=\widehat{\mathcal{F}}_1(u,q_1,q_2|Z),\qquad \mathcal{F}_{\lozenge}(u,q_1,q_2|Z)=(1-q_2q_1Z^{1/2})\widehat{\mathcal{F}}_0(u,q_1,q_2|Z).
$$

This extends the bilinear relations from $q_1=q^{-1}$ and $q_2=q$ to generic parameters in the indicated sector; the supplied text gives no separate resolution status.

336592.title: Extremal growth-rate conjecture for polymorphic valence sequences
336592.literal_statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a polymorphic valence sequence. Let $\mathscr{T}_\sigma$ be the set of isomorphism classes of face-homogeneous tessellations with valence sequence $\sigma$, and define

$$
\underline{\lambda}_\sigma=\inf\{\gamma(T):T\in\mathscr{T}_\sigma\},\qquad
\overline{\lambda}_\sigma=\sup\{\gamma(T):T\in\mathscr{T}_\sigma\}.
$$

Also set

$$
\mathscr{L}_\sigma=\{T\in\mathscr{T}_\sigma:\gamma(T)=\underline{\lambda}_\sigma\},\qquad
\mathscr{H}_\sigma=\{T\in\mathscr{T}_\sigma:\gamma(T)=\overline{\lambda}_\sigma\}.
$$

**Extremal growth-rate conjecture.** The sets $\mathscr{L}_\sigma$ and $\mathscr{H}_\sigma$ are nonempty. Thus the lower and upper growth-rate bounds are realized by tessellations with valence sequence $\sigma$. The source presents this as an open conjecture and gives no resolution.

336833.title: Ayyer–Klee–Schilling conjecture on linear eigenvalues of promotion matrices
336833.literal_statement: Let $P$ be a poset of size $n$ that is not a down forest, and let $M^{P}$ be its promotion transition matrix. For each element $x$ of $P$, call an element $y$ a **successor** of $x$ when $x\prec y$. Suppose that every eigenvalue of $M^{P}$ is linear in the parameters $x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}$. **Ayyer–Klee–Schilling conjecture.** Then: (1) the coefficients of the parameters in the eigenvalues are all in $\{-1,1\}$; (2) every element of $P$ has at most two successors; and (3) the only parameters whose coefficients in the eigenvalues are $-1$ are those corresponding either to elements with two successors or to elements having a successor with two successors. This conjecture seeks to classify non-down-forest posets whose promotion matrices have linear eigenvalues; the stated necessary conditions are motivated by examples such as the rank-two ladder, but the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.

336980.title: Laurent irreducibility conjecture for toric-digraph R-systems
336980.literal_statement:

**Toric-digraph Laurent irreducibility conjecture.** The rational functions $Y_v(t)$ are pairwise coprime irreducible polynomials in $\mathbf{x}_V$; more precisely, they are irreducible and coprime as Laurent polynomials, up to monomial factors.

This is the Laurent phenomenon suggested by the authors' computations. They additionally conjecture that these Laurent polynomials are actual polynomials, but the supplied statement asserts pairwise coprimality and irreducibility in the Laurent setting.

337213.title: Korpelainen–Lozin–Razgon conjecture on labelled well-quasi-ordering of graph classes
337213.literal_statement:
Let a graph class be **well-quasi-ordered (wqo)** by the induced subgraph relation if it contains no infinite antichain under that relation, and let it be **labelled well-quasi-ordered (lwqo)** if the analogous property holds for graphs whose vertices are labelled by elements of every wqo label set. A graph class is defined by finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs when its set of minimal graphs excluded as induced subgraphs is finite.

**Korpelainen–Lozin–Razgon conjecture.** A class of graphs which is wqo by the induced subgraph relation is lwqo if and only if it is defined by finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs.

Every lwqo graph class is wqo and defined by finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, so the conjecture asserts the converse implication as well. The paper disproves this conjecture by constructing a class of permutation graphs that is wqo and has finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs but is not lwqo.

337263.title: EL-labeling criterion for factorization posets
337263.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a group generated as a monoid by a conjugation-closed subset $A$, let $\mathfrak{c}\in G$, and let $A_{\mathfrak{c}}$ be the generators appearing in reduced $A$-factorizations of $\mathfrak{c}$. Let $\mathcal{P}_{\mathfrak{c}}(G,A)$ be the factorization poset, and let $\lambda_{\mathfrak{c}}$ be its natural labeling. A linear order of $A_{\mathfrak{c}}$ is **$\mathfrak{c}$-compatible** in the sense defined for the factorization poset. **EL-labeling conjecture.** The natural labeling $\lambda_{\mathfrak{c}}$ is an EL-labeling of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathfrak{c}}(G,A)$ with respect to some linear order $\prec$ of $A_{\mathfrak{c}}$ if and only if $\mathcal{P}_{\mathfrak{c}}(G,A)$ is totally chain-connected and $\prec$ is $\mathfrak{c}$-compatible. This reformulates the preceding unique-rising-chain conjecture in terms of EL-labelings.

337457.title: Elementary-divisor conjecture for critical groups of induced representations
337457.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian group of order $r$, let $\mathfrak{S}$ denote the tower of symmetric groups, and consider the differential tower of groups $A\wr\mathfrak{S}$. For $k\leq n$, let $V(U^kD^k)_n$ be the induced representation corresponding to $U^kD^k$, and let $p_j$ denote the rank sizes. Write $e_i$ for the non-unit elementary divisors of the critical group $K(V(D^kU^k)_{n-k})$. **Elementary-divisor conjecture.** The critical group

$$
K(V(U^kD^k)_n)=K\left(\operatorname{Ind}_{A\wr\mathfrak{S}_{n-k}}^{A\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}\mathbbm{1}\right)
$$

is given, as a list of elementary divisors, by

$$
\left(1^{p_{n-k}},\left(r^{k}\frac{n!}{(n-k)!}\right)^{p_n-2p_{n-k}+p_{n-2k}},r^{k}\frac{n!}{(n-k)!}e_i\right),
$$

where exponents involving rank sizes denote multiplicities. This predicts the precise elementary-divisor structure of these critical groups in the wreath-product differential tower.

337478.title: The winding-number conjecture for dilated simplex Ehrhart h*-vectors
337478.literal_statement:
Let $\Delta_r^n=\{x\in[0,r]^n:\sum x_i=r\}$ be the $(n-1)$-dimensional simplex, and call a decorated ordered set partition $((L_1)_{l_1},\ldots,(L_k)_{l_k})$ **simplicial** when $1\le l_i\le r-1$ and $\sum_i l_i=r$. For a simplicial ordered set partition with $1\in L_1$, let $w_P$ denote its winding number. Denote by $m_0,m_1,\ldots$ the numbers of such partitions having winding numbers $w_P=0,1,2,\ldots$. **The dilated-simplex winding-number conjecture.** The vector $(m_0,m_1,\ldots)$ equals the Ehrhart $h^*$-vector of $\Delta_r^n$, and is obtained from the generating series 
$$
\sum_{s=0}^{\infty}\binom{n-1+rs}{n-1}x^s.
$$
 The conjecture proposes a combinatorial interpretation of the Ehrhart $h^*$-vector, extending the computationally observed winding-number enumeration for dilated simplices.

340343.title: The Schmidt–White conjecture on cyclotomic strongly regular graphs
340343.literal_statement: Let $q=p^{\ell}$ be a prime power, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $N$ divide $(q^m-1)/(q-1)$. Let $C_0^{(N,q^m)}$ be the subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^*$ of index $N$, and let $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_{q^m},C_0^{(N,q^m)})$ denote the Cayley graph with connection set $C_0^{(N,q^m)}$. A graph is **strongly regular** if it is regular and every pair of adjacent vertices and every pair of nonadjacent vertices have respectively constant numbers of common neighbors. **The Schmidt–White conjecture.** Assume that $N\mid(q^m-1)/(q-1)$. Then $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_{q^m},C_0^{(N,q^m)})$ is strongly regular if and only if it is either a subfield example, a semi-primitive example, or one of the eleven sporadic examples in Table 1 of the source. This conjecture aims to classify the cyclotomic strongly regular graphs; the source states that it remains open, while the stated necessary-and-sufficient conditions provide a way to search for further examples.
